Runs clean (243 rows, 1 models line by baseWith, 2 declared absent). It requires every GW 'Unit: Model' row of each datasheet in a unit (stats row on that guide line, a models line by name or wargear on GW's base, or an absent declaration), checks every baseWith against a GW wargear row with the same base, and flags unused declarations; mutation tests confirm each path. Minor limits, not blocking: (1) an `absent` declaration covers every unit of that datasheet, not one unit; (2) a models line's baseWith is looked up across all the unit's stats rows, not only the row baseOf() picks; (3) a line counts as a match when all the words of the row's model are in its name, so a wargear name inside a model name also counts. With today's lists none of these changes a result.

The new step returns 'Tankbustas: Boss Nob' for Nob (the only row whose model contains it, no variant). It returns null instead of the unit's own row when a model name shares a word with a model row of its unit, or when the only row is a variant: Boyz/Nob gives null rather than '(Armageddon)'. Breaka Boyz/Nob gives 'Breaka Boyz: Boss Nob'. 'A/B: Model' rows are split for both units, and models are split on ' / '. declared() now throws on a missing guide row. Absent entries (no `row`) can't be matched by declared() by mistake (norm(undefined) is ''). Over all 243 rows my own matching against the guide agrees with every base: 207 exact, 12 model, 1 part-of-name, 7 plural, 4 words, 2 model-of, 10 declared.
